what.text: This page follows refugees from South Africa living in Angola, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 1993, the last year with a figure, UNHCR counted 168 South African refugees in Angola, 1.8% of all refugees from South Africa that year.
Today, Ireland hosts the most South African refugees, followed by Canada, France and the United Kingdom.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of South Africa with the ANC from 1981 to 1983 and 1985 to 1988.
It also records armed conflict over Namibia territory with SWAPO from 1973 to 1989.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group runs from 1978, at 1000 refugees, to 1993.
The figure was at its highest, 10000, at the end of 1986 and 1987; the main years of displacement in the data are 1980 to 1988.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in Angola.
These are year-end totals for Angola only, reported to UNHCR from 1978 to 1993.
